seoTitle: How to Join a Channel in Slack (2026 Guide)
metaDescription: Browse and join public Slack channels through Directories, filter down to the ones you haven't joined, and join temporarily when you only need short-term access.
intro: Staying connected to the right project rooms and department updates gets harder as a Slack workspace grows past a handful of channels. This guide covers where the full channel list lives in Slack's current layout, how to tell which ones you're already in, how to filter down to just the channels you haven't joined, and a lesser-known option for joining a channel only temporarily.

steps.heading: Start from your Channels list in the sidebar
steps.body: The left sidebar shows a Channels section listing every room you've already joined, with an Add channels link underneath for anything new. This is your home base for daily use, but it only shows channels you're in; it won't surface public rooms you haven't joined, which is why finding new ones means going somewhere else in the app. Below Channels you'll also see Direct messages and any installed apps, sharing the same sidebar space.

image.caption: The sidebar's Channels section, listing the rooms you've already joined with an Add channels link for finding more.

steps.heading: Open Directories and switch to the Channels tab
steps.body: From Home, click Directories, then select the Channels tab. This is the full-workspace channel list, separate from the short one in your sidebar. Each row shows the channel name, member count, a short description, and whether you've already joined it. A Create Channel button sits next to the search bar if none of the existing ones fit.

image.caption: The Directories panel's Channels tab — the real browsable list, showing member counts, descriptions, and Joined status per channel.

steps.heading: Filter the list down to channels you haven't joined
steps.body: The dropdown above the list defaults to All channels, which mixes ones you're in with ones you're not. Switch it to Other channels to see only the rooms you haven't joined, or My channels to confirm what you're already a member of. On a workspace with dozens of channels this narrows things fast, without reading every description.

image.caption: The channel list filter dropdown, switching between All channels, My channels, and Other channels.

steps.heading: Check a channel's description before joining
steps.body: Each row in the directory carries a one-line description set by whoever created the channel. Read it before joining, since names alone can be ambiguous on a busy workspace. A channel marked Required is mandatory for everyone in the workspace, and members generally can't leave it; anything without that tag is optional. If the purpose still isn't clear, open the channel directly and skim recent messages before committing.

steps.heading: Join the channel and confirm it in your sidebar
steps.body: Click a channel's row, or its Join button on rooms you haven't joined, to add it to your account. It appears back in your sidebar's Channels list immediately, and in most workspaces you can scroll back through its full message history from before you joined. If it's a channel you only need briefly, click the arrow next to Join instead and pick Just for today, For 48 hours, or For 1 week; Slack drops you from it automatically once that period ends, and it lists it under a separate Temporary channels section in the meantime. If your sidebar feels cluttered after joining several channels, drag them into custom sections to group them by project or team.

faq.question: Can I join a private channel the same way?
faq.answer: No, private channels don't appear in the public Directories list. You need an invite or request from an existing member to get into one.

faq.question: How do I leave a channel later?
faq.answer: Open the channel, click its name at the top, and choose Leave channel from the details menu, unless it's marked Required, in which case you likely can't.

faq.question: What does joining a channel temporarily do?
faq.answer: Picking a duration (a day, 48 hours, or a week) from the arrow next to a channel's Join button adds you for that window only. Slack removes you automatically once it's up, and the channel sits in a Temporary channels section of your sidebar until then.

faq.question: Can I organize joined channels into custom sections?
faq.answer: Yes, drag any channel in your sidebar into a custom section, or create a new section from the Channels header's options menu.

faq.question: Will I see message history from before I joined?
faq.answer: Yes, in most workspaces new members can scroll back through a public channel's full history once they join.

faq.question: What's the difference between 'All channels' and 'Other channels' in the filter?
faq.answer: All channels shows everything in the workspace regardless of membership. Other channels narrows that list to only the ones you haven't joined yet.
